concepts.def: A computer design in which programs and data are stored together in the same memory, fetched by the CPU using the same buses.
The control unit decodes instructions and coordinates the processor, while the arithmetic logic unit performs calculations and logical comparisons.
Tiny, very fast stores in the CPU: the PC holds the next instruction's address, the MAR an address, the MDR data, and the accumulator results.
The repeated cycle in which the CPU fetches an instruction from memory, decodes it, and executes it, with the program counter then updated.
Clock speed, the number of cores and the amount of cache all affect how much work a processor can complete each second.
A computer built into a larger device, such as a washing machine, with dedicated software performing one fixed set of functions.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Systems Architecture — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Systems Architecture brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Systems Architecture.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Is an embedded system just a small general-purpose computer?
options: Yes - embedded just means the computer is screwed into a case.
Yes - the program counter counts how many programs are open.
Yes - an embedded system can run any program you install.
No - an embedded system runs dedicated software for one fixed function inside a device; you cannot install new applications on it like a PC.

mcqs.q: Does doubling the number of cores double a computer's speed?
options: No - software must be written to split work across cores, and many tasks cannot be parallelised, so the gain is usually less than double.
Yes - two cores always means exactly twice the performance.
Yes - each extra core doubles speed again automatically.
Yes - embedded just means the computer is screwed into a case.

mcqs.q: Does the program counter hold the data currently being processed?
options: Yes - the program counter counts how many programs are open.
Yes - embedded just means the computer is screwed into a case.
No - the program counter holds the ADDRESS of the next instruction to fetch; data being processed sits in registers such as the accumulator and MDR.
Yes - the program counter stores whatever the CPU is working on.
